chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Barqi, raising it from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I asked him about having intercourse with women in their hindquarters (rectum). He said: 'There is no harm in it, but I dislike that you do it.' And the report which we previously mentioned from al-Rida (peace be upon him), and his saying 'We do not do that,' is evidence of the dislike of that, according to what we said. It also bears the possibility that the two reports came for the purpose of Taqiyya (dissimulation), because none of the general public (Sunni scholars) permits that except what is narrated from Malik, and his companions differ with him regarding it.

key_terms.أَعْقَازُ: Hindquarters / rear ends (specifically the rectum in this context)
key_terms.الْعَامَّةُ: The general public (often referring to Sunni scholars in Shia texts)
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَةٌ: Dislike (recommended to avoid but not forbidden)
key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on anal intercourse with one's wife?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the juristic status of *al-wath' bi-l-dubur* (anal intercourse) with one's wife, establishing it as permissible (*mubah*) yet disliked (*makruh*) based on Imam al-Rida's (AS) statement. The text highlights a scholarly nuance: while the permissibility is affirmed, the dislike may stem from *Taqiyya* (dissimulation) to align with the majority of Sunni schools who generally prohibit it, except for the Hanafi school's allowance. This reflects the Shia tradition of balancing intrinsic permissibility with social prudence in marital relations.
